newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin warns Chechens against one-sided decisions.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin warns Chechens against one-sided decisions.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Friday urged Chechnya's new leader to work for peace in the rebel region and, clearly cautioning him against secessionist moves, told him not to make any "one-sided decisions".

"There can be no ons-sided decisions in our relations," Yeltsin said in a radio address. He was speaking two days after former guerrilla leader Aslan Maskhadov was sworn in as Chechen president after a nearly two-year conflict with Russian troops.
Yeltsin, 66, spoke clearly but slowly and sounded hoarse in his first radio address to the Russian people since he fell ill with pneumonia last month.
Maskhadov has pledged to push on with Chechnya's demands to break away from Russia. Moscow has repeatedly said it will not allow the mainly Moslem region in southern Russia to secede.
Yeltsin said Maskhadov should concentrate on sorting out problems within Chechnya, which also contains ethnic Russians.
"A great responsibility lies with the leadership of Chehcnya," Yeltsin declared.
